CausalLink.description: Only explicit causal references belong here. Cleanup/audit failures stay in domain results.

ConfigCommitRequest.description: Compare-and-swap request for applying a complete set of source-tree changes.

ConfigContentType.description: Source content kinds accepted by the Workspace configuration tree.

ConfigEntry.description: One source entry in the Workspace configuration tree.

authoring_source.description: Completion-only shape for partial values; never materialized as defaults.

ConfigTreeChange.description: Base-relative change applied by a Workspace configuration commit.

ConfigurationFailureDetails.description: The complete wire allowlist. No path, import, identifier or diagnostic is a field.

ConfigurationFailureReason.description: Observed causes only. These do not grant retries or establish an adoption result.

oneOf.description: Retained unknown/corrupt evidence is not forwarded or replaced by a made-up cause.

ConfigurationPublicationOutcome.description:
Observed means queue admission, projection availability, or Runtime acknowledgement,
depending on stage. It never confirms model processing or current policy application.

oneOf.description: No matching evidence was observed. This is not permission to change the ID.

state.description:
Before the first adoption this is an editable, evaluated migration draft.
source_stored distinguishes it from the unchanged stored source.

legacy_constraints.description: Exact retained domain restrictions, not editable payloads on permission keys.

CorrelationRef.description: Correlation is deliberately a distinct field/type from operation identity.

FailureContext.description: Common metadata is untrusted after deserialization. No audience label confers trust.

causes.description: Ordered immediate-to-root chain, at most four references; never recursive payloads.

FailureEnvelope_ConfigurationFailureDeta.description: DTO/schema source only. Deserialization does not produce a ProjectedFailure.

FailureEnvelope_RuntimeControlCause.description: DTO/schema source only. Deserialization does not produce a ProjectedFailure.

NamespaceDeclaration.description:
This input deliberately has no owner field. The Host supplies the registered
identity/namespace handle independently of guest-controlled declaration data.

operation_ref.description: A reference, not an idempotency/retry grant. Disclosure remains domain-owned.

PermissionAssignment.description:
`None` at the consuming policy boundary means unset. An empty assignment is
explicit deny-all; this crate never chooses or reinstates a default.

PermissionReference.description: The discriminant, not an identifier's spelling, selects a reference kind.

oneOf.description:
Authorizes operation use, not a target Worker or a Workspace collection.
The Worker Feature must still enforce its directional target control grant.

ProblemDetails_ConfigurationFailureDetai.description: Untrusted wire DTO. Unknown RFC extensions are ignored; yoi_failure is mandatory here.

RepositoryApiError.description: Error body shared by the existing repository routes and their generated adapters.

failure.description:
An origin-projected error-contract attachment, not raw HTTP error text.
Receiving it does not authorize redisclosure to a different audience.

ScopedPermission.description:
Stored scopes retain their original resources and exact operation names.

A legacy Worker read adapter may use [`canonical_worker_operation`] to project
operation use, but must retain the original target separately for the Worker
Feature's control-grant check, including direction, revocation and delegation
limits. Replacing an old Worker resource with WorkerOperation and discarding
that target would broaden authority. Neither validation nor `covers` performs
that conversion.

StartupFailureAttachment.description:
A bounded, projected envelope at the Worker/Runtime or metadata boundary.
No constructor accepts Display text, arbitrary JSON fields, or an unprojected error.

WorkspaceConfigTreeResponse.description: Workspace configuration tree plus the exact evaluation contract that produced it.
